abstract.text:
We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of
motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and
that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place
in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate
effective Hamiltonian.

In this section, repeating the arguments [30], we shall attempt to demonstrate that the presence of YM
BPS ansatz f 1 BP S, (1.8), in the (Minkowskian) YMH BPS monopole theory violates manifestly the CP
invariance of that theory.

The same effect CP violating occurs, as we have demonstrated in the previous section, in the YMH
model involving BPS magnetic monopoles (without any θ-dependense). The crucial point here is the
presence of the BPS ansatz f 1 BP S, (1.8), in that model (as it can be seen from (2.16)).
The argument leans on Dirac quantization, the dyon-charge analysis of Witten, and an analogy with superfluid helium II.

The starting point of our discussion will be the well known Dirac quantization condition [27] for the
electric and magnetic charges presented in a closed system of quantum fields.

So the allowed values of magnetic monopoles (if latter ones are contemplated in the model: for instance
if Higgs modes are present in such model, violating the initial SU (2) gauge symmetry) are not integer if
θ 6 = 0.

Indeed, there can be drawn a highly transparent parallel between the Minkowskian YMH vacuum
involving vacuum BPS monopole solutions and a liquid helium II specimen described in the Bogolubov-
Landau model [17].

While in the Bogolubov-Landau model [17] of liquid helium II this comes to repulsion forces between
helium atoms as the cause of superfluidity effects, in the Minkowskian YMH vacuum involving BPS
monopole solutions, the cause of the superfluidity taking place is in the strong YMH coupling g (entering
effectively the appropriate action functional (1.1)).
Finally, the discussion turns to Dirac fundamental quantization, which is claimed to restore a P- and C-invariant description.
This us demonstrated CP conservation is the next in turn remarkable feature of that model.

In this section, repeating the arguments [30], we shall attempt to demonstrate that the presence of YM
BPS ansatz f 1 BP S, (1.8), in the (Minkowskian) YMH BPS monopole theory violates manifestly the CP
invariance of that theory.

The same effect CP violating occurs, as we have demonstrated in the previous section, in the YMH
model involving BPS magnetic monopoles (without any θ-dependense). The crucial point here is the
presence of the BPS ansatz f 1 BP S, (1.8), in that model (as it can be seen from (2.16)).
The argument leans on Dirac quantization, the dyon-charge analysis of Witten, and an analogy with superfluid helium II.

The starting point of our discussion will be the well known Dirac quantization condition [27] for the
electric and magnetic charges presented in a closed system of quantum fields.

So the allowed values of magnetic monopoles (if latter ones are contemplated in the model: for instance
if Higgs modes are present in such model, violating the initial SU (2) gauge symmetry) are not integer if

Indeed, there can be drawn a highly transparent parallel between the Minkowskian YMH vacuum
involving vacuum BPS monopole solutions and a liquid helium II specimen described in the Bogolubov-
Landau model [17].

While in the Bogolubov-Landau model [17] of liquid helium II this comes to repulsion forces between
helium atoms as the cause of superfluidity effects, in the Minkowskian YMH vacuum involving BPS
monopole solutions, the cause of the superfluidity taking place is in the strong YMH coupling g (entering
effectively the appropriate action functional (1.1)).
Finally, the discussion turns to Dirac fundamental quantization, which is claimed to restore a P- and C-invariant description.
